dedupe_keys.name: human failure in chemical plant accidents in south korea 2010 to 2017 classification from investigation reports

description: This case study analyses chemical accidents caused by human failure in South Korea between 2010 and 2017, using the official accident investigation reports, and classifies each failure as an error or a violation under the human failure scheme of the UK Health and Safety Executive. It finds that several kinds of human failure acting together were a more important cause than any one alone, and names incorrect application of process rules and procedures, inadequate chemical information such as safety data sheets, lack of training and gaps in current safety regulation as the main causes, with individual accidents described as examples. It was written by Seungho Jung, Seungkyoo Pak, Kwanwoo Lee and Chankyu Kang and published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health on 26 October 2021. Coverage is South Korea. The article is available free online under CC BY 4.0; its data availability statement says not applicable, so no accident table is released. Caveats: only accidents attributed to human failure were analysed, and the classification relies on the reports' own findings. For simulation it gives failure mechanisms and their mix for human reliability terms in accident frequency, plant operation and cascading failure models of chemical sites. It is related to the Korean chemical plant accident probability index record in this catalogue.
